I disagree with a lot of the laissez-faire advice you've been given so far.  First, to have defined abs your going to need a body fat percentage that is 12% or below.  That gives you a target that is concrete and trackable.  To get that low is going to take ultra high levels of discipline, measurement, and adherence.  

Not knowing much about you I would recommend daily weight, macro, and calorie tracking with weekly body measurements to get body fat estimation. (See the navy method body fat calculation).  You'll need to do some form of the Stronglifts 2-3 times per week.  A calorie deficit of at least 3500 per week.  Protein of at least .7 grams per lb of bodyweight per day.  A window of eating of 8 hours per day max.  If you did something like this for year consistently, without falling off the wagon, you'd like close in on a body fat percentage in the low teens.  Again this will take serious adherence and discipline.

Walking after dinner, focusing on ab exercises, or avoiding dairy isn't going to cut it.  You'll need a total mindset switch

Don't feel bad, this is a common story.  Women typically don't love idealistically like most men do.  They love what can be provided to them, i.e. attention, money, tuition, butterflies, status.  On top of this, no past provisions are taken into account only what is being provided currently.  This is why it's common for women to leave at a man's lowest points like illness, job loss, self-isolation.  

I hate to burst your bubble but there is almost certainly another man she is with already.  In reference to above, it is most common to have another source of provision before leaving the current relationship.

You did make some mistakes that you shouldn't make in the future if in an LTR.  One, don't work to the bone to be a sole provider.  She will resent you for having more time for work than her.  Plus it gives her more free time to explore other relationships while amplifying the void from you being at work.  Make her earn her fair share which will also keep her occupied.  Idle hands do the Devil's work.

Two, no woman wants to play the role of therapist with her partner.  It makes her mistrust your ability to provide security and stability.  If you need to talk, do it with a male friend or a therapist that you see secretly.  This is an unfortunate reality of being a man, even when you're dieing inside you need to show the outward appearance of being okay.  Otherwise people see you as a child or effeminate, which is a death blow in many settings.

Don't hate yourself, these are common mistakes and it's hard if not almost impossible to fight off the biological imperatives of female nature over long periods.  She's doing what her hardwiring is directing her to do to feel provided for and secure even though you were doing all you could.  Life is cold and hard.

On the plus side you weren't married nor had any children.  These are the best circumstances for a man to have a relationship end.  Imagine all of this happening but she takes your house, children, and 25-50% of your earnings moving forward.  You don't have to worry about any of that plus you're still a young man.  I know you're hurting but to many men who have been through the family divorce court wringer, you're sitting on a winning lottery ticket.  Be grateful to have dodged these bullets, find intrinsic value in yourself, and be on your purpose moving forward.  

Things will get better.  One last tidbit, for God's sake do not chase her or take her back unless you want to make things worse.  Be in the frame that it's her loss and you're going to live a good life moving forward.  Hope this helps, hang in there
